newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Long bond yields breached the key 15 percent level in late Friday trade, buoyed by gains on the U.S. market where the 30 year T-bond broke below seven percent after more-subdued-than-expected August U.S. CPI data.
Shortly after 1400 GMT the yields on the R150 was at 14.98 percent from 15.13 percent previously.
"The market was buoyed in the afternoon by gains on the U.S. market where the yield on the U.S. long bond broke below seven percent after the release of subdued CPI data," a bond trader said.
The 30 year T-bond was last trading below seven percent at 6.96 percent.

"I expect the strong run to follow through at the start of next week. The 15 percent level was a key one and the market is eyeing 14.75 percent as the next important level on the downside," the dealer added.

Bond yields initially moved higher in sympathy with a weaker rand but recovered losses at around noon after the Finance Department revised April to August revenue figures up to 55.56 bln rand from 50.37 billion, sparking good offshore and local interest.

The finance department said it had revised up its estimate of April-August revenue following a miscalculation due to software errors. The department also revised data for April to August last year to 49.273 billion rand from the 48.564 billion rand originally stated.
Dealers said the revision had helped buoy sentiment which was then given an additional boost as the U.S. Treasury market rallied.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net sellers of 21.36 million rand worth of South African bonds on Thursday after buying 110.88 million rand on Wednesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were 39.51 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement date -- from 7.3 billion rand on Wednesday.
The rand ended below 4.50 on the dollar after a relatively quiet day, dealers said.
At 1428 GMT it was quoted at 4.4980/5030 against the dollar from 4.4990/5040 late on Thursday.
Dealers said the unit held above the 4.50 barrier in early Friday trade as importer demand for dollars continued to weigh on the currency.
They said the day had been marked by good two-way flows with exporters at the higher levels.
In the absence of fresh economic news, the rand was expected to trade in a narrow 4.48 to 5.5150 band at the start of next week.
Against the crosses, the currency was trading at 6.9937/7.0006 against sterling from 6.9959/0069 on Thursday and at 0.3357/3360 marks from 0.3362/3367 marks previously.

On the money market, three-month NCDs were slightly lower at between 15.80 to 15.95 percent from 15.80 and 16.00 percent while 90-day BAs were also slightly lower at between 15.20 to 15.45 percent from 15.25 and 15.45 percent.
The Reserve Bank said the daily shortage eased to 8.043 billion rand on Thursday from 8.196 billion rand on Wednesday.
